summary: The main article describes a nickel- and photoredox-catalyzed decarboxylative aminocarbonylation of aryl bromides using oxamic acids. It includes optimization tables for reaction conditions and deuteration, schemes for substrate scope and mechanism, and a section on the synthesis of deuterated formamides.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Classical Synthetic Routes and Photoredox-Catalytic Approaches toward Amides
items.description: Compares traditional amidation methods with modern photoredox-catalyzed strategies using various carbamoyl radical precursors.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of the Reaction Conditions
items.description: Lists the screening of photocatalysts, bases, solvents, and concentrations to optimize the yield of the aminocarbonylation reaction.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Substrate Scope
items.description: Displays the variety of oxamic acids and aryl bromides compatible with the optimized reaction conditions, including a gram-scale example.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Proposed Mechanism
items.description: Illustrates the dual catalytic cycle involving photoredox-mediated decarboxylation and nickel-catalyzed cross-coupling.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Deuterated Formamide Synthesis: Optimization
items.description: Details the optimization of conditions for synthesizing deuterated formamides using a HAT catalyst and D2O.

items.heading: Scheme 4
items.caption: Preparation of Deuterated Formamides
items.description: Shows the scope of various oxamic acids converted into deuterated formamides with high deuterium incorporation.
